datasets.name: EEG during Balinese dance movements and balance tasks in expert dancers and non-dancers
datasets.description: Raw 16-channel EEG from 38 women (23 expert Balinese dancers and 15 non-dancers) recorded in a single session with two paradigms: three Balinese dance movements (ngeed, agem right, agem left) and a Romberg-type standing task. The dataset includes a separate resting recording, manually annotated movement-phase events, and Standing Stork balance times in the participants file. It supports research on cortical activity, motor expertise and postural balance in traditional dancers.
datasets.authors: I Putu Adiartha Griadhi, Nila Wahyuni, Indira Vidiari Juhanna, Ida Ayu Astiti Suadnyana
datasets.eeg_reference: Ipsilateral earlobe: A1 for left-hemisphere and A2 for right-hemisphere sites
datasets.placement_scheme: International 10-20 system, 16 scalp sites, no midline electrodes

datasets.name: Cognitive overload and rest dataset. Simultaneous EEG + PPG + ECG + eye-tracking
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw 64-channel EEG recorded simultaneously with electrocardiography, photoplethysmography, eye-tracking/pupillometry, and behavioral data from 124 healthy young adults. Recordings were made during a resting-state session (alternating eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks followed by passive cartoon viewing) and an adaptive verbal working memory digit-span task with serial recall. The dataset supports research on cognitive load, working memory, and psychophysiological correlates of mental effort.
datasets.authors: Yuri G. Pavlov

datasets.name: EgoBrain-Mini: egocentric video, 32-channel EEG, wrist/arm IMU and audio during everyday actions (40 adults)
datasets.description: EgoBrain-Mini is a BIDS conversion of the lightweight egocentric release of EgoBrain. It provides synchronized first-person video, 32-channel EEG, four body-worn IMUs and audio from 40 adults performing 39 everyday seated actions (1,562 sub-actions, about 63 hours of EEG). The dataset supports research on multimodal human action understanding and brain-vision alignment. EEG values, audio, and video are unchanged from the original release, which is preserved under sourcedata.
datasets.authors: Nie Lin, Yansen Wang, Dongqi Han, Weibang Jiang, Jingyuan Li, Ryosuke Furuta, Yoichi Sato, Dongsheng Li
datasets.eeg_reference: CMS/DRL reference sensors placed on the earlobes using EMOTIV ear clips (EMOTIV FLEX 2 Gel)

datasets.name: Spell-IT-Out
datasets.description: Spell-IT-Out is an EEG dataset of 25 native Italian speakers who listened to sentences, repeated them, and then produced them syllable by syllable at a fixed pace, either aloud (overt) or silently (covert). Each participant completed 3 overt and 3 covert runs of 20 trials. Recordings used 61 EEG channels plus 1 EOG channel at 2048 Hz. Hand-corrected word and syllable timings of overt speech are provided as events, and derivatives include preprocessed continuous EEG and syllable epochs for machine learning.
datasets.authors: Tommaso Cortecchia, Stefano Tortora, Jeff Kiesner, Emanuele Menegatti, Luca Tonin

datasets.name: Mapping effective connectivity of human amygdala with intracranial stimulation - es-TT evoked potentials
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG evoked-potential epochs recorded during single-pulse electrical stimulation of the amygdala (electrical stimulation tract-tracing, es-TT) in 11 neurosurgical patients. The dataset comprises 46 stimulation runs of epoched recordings from depth, strip and grid electrodes, supporting mapping of effective connectivity of the human amygdala. It is a BIDS conversion of data originally released on OSF for Sawada et al., 2022.
datasets.authors: Hiroyuki Oya, LeiQi

datasets.name: Sensory-guided joint-learning MI-BCI study
datasets.description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recordings from 39 healthy, BCI-naive participants in a longitudinal motor imagery brain-computer interface study of sensory-guided human-machine joint learning. Participants performed online 1D and 2D cursor control with left-hand, right-hand, bilateral-hand and rest imagery across multiple sessions. The cohorts were joint learning with tactile guidance and EEGNet adaptation, a fixed BCI2000 decoder control, a tactile-only control, and an EEGNet control. The data are trial-segmented and were reorganized in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Hanwen Wang, Yisha Zhang, Maxim Karrenbach, Yidan Ding, Bin He

datasets.name: A Fine-grained Spatiotemporal ECoG Dataset during Speech Perception in Tonal Language
datasets.description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from patients during speech perception in a tonal language (Mandarin), collected at Huashan Hospital. The BIDS version provides the 70-150 Hz Hilbert high-gamma envelope, not raw voltage, converted from NWB to EDF. It supports research on the fine-grained spatiotemporal neural dynamics of tone and speech processing.
datasets.authors: Haobo Zhang, Daohan Zhang, Jinsong Wu, Yuanning Li, Junfeng Lu

datasets.name: Human STN LFP during a stop-signal task (STN delta)
datasets.description: Intraoperative local field potential recordings from the subthalamic nucleus of 13 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. Signals were acquired with microelectrodes while patients performed a stop-signal reaction time task. This derivative release repackages the authors' filtered 250 Hz continuous LFP (0.5 Hz high-pass version) in BIDS format with event annotations.
datasets.authors: Johanna Petra Szabo, Panna Hegedüs, Tamás Laszlovszky, László Halász, Gabriella Miklós, Bálint Király, György Perczel, Virág Bokodi, László Entz, István Ulbert, Gertrúd Tamás, Dániel Fabó, Loránd Erőss, Balázs Hangya

datasets.name: Basketball Motor Imagery EEG Dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 35 healthy participants performing three basketball-related motor observation and motor imagery tasks: single-handed dribbling, two-handed ball passing, and two-person passing. The dataset provides raw EEG, preprocessed data, and phase locking value (PLV) functional connectivity results. It supports research on motor imagery, action observation, and inter-brain connectivity in sport-related contexts.
datasets.authors: Jiahui Han, Jiaqi Wang, Lingrong Jia, Ming Tang, School of Physics and Electronic Technology, Liaoning Normal University, Institute of Psychological and Brain Sciences, Liaoning Normal University

datasets.name: Simultaneous EEG-SEEG recordings of deep mesial temporal sources
datasets.description: This dataset contains nine simultaneous scalp EEG and stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings of mesial temporal networks from seven patients with temporal lobe epilepsy. For each network, the earliest and highest-amplitude interictal intracerebral spikes were marked, and 1 s epochs centred on the spike peak are provided for both SEEG and scalp EEG channels. The data support research on how deep mesial temporal sources contribute to scalp EEG and on detecting them non-invasively.
datasets.authors: Laurent Koessler, Eric Ternisien, Thierry Cecchin, Sophie Colnat-Coulbois, Louis Maillard

datasets.name: PerezBlanco2026: Wrist-motion (4-direction pointing) motor-execution dataset
datasets.description: A multimodal dataset of wrist pointing movements recorded from 45 healthy participants performing a four-direction task (flexion, extension, radial deviation, ulnar deviation) with a 3-DoF wrist exoskeleton. It includes 8-channel EEG over sensorimotor areas and 8-channel EMG, with continuous visual cursor feedback. The recordings are intended for biomarker research and for brain-computer interface and rehabilitation applications.
datasets.authors: Jorge German Perez Blanco, Javier Mauricio Antelis Ortiz, Luis Guillermo Hernandez Rojas, Hector Lizarraga Torreblanca

datasets.name: Human subthalamic nucleus microelectrode recordings during an interrupted reach task (London et al., 2021)
datasets.description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the subthalamic nucleus of patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. Patients performed an extended touchscreen reaching task in which the target sometimes changed mid-movement (interrupted reach). The dataset contains wideband raw signals from tungsten microelectrodes and macro contacts, with digital event markers, from 8 subjects across 16 task blocks.
datasets.authors: Dennis London, Arash Fazl, Kalman Katlowitz, Marisol Soula, Michael Pourfar, Alon Mogilner, Roozbeh Kiani

datasets.name: DBS microelectrode recordings from 132 patients, University Clinical Centre Gdańsk (Osowska, Szymański, Libionka 2026; derivative: authors' band-passed, classifier-selected MER segments)
datasets.description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings (MER) from 132 patients undergoing awake deep brain stimulation surgery at the University Clinical Centre in Gdańsk, Poland. Patients had Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, dystonia, tremor and other movement disorders, or epilepsy. Up to five parallel microelectrodes were advanced toward the MRI-planned target, recording at successive depths. This derivative release contains band-pass filtered (500-5000 Hz) short segments selected by a Random Forest signal-quality classifier, plus 29 expert-annotated excerpts of striatum/putamen, GPe and GPi. Data are repackaged in BIDS as BrainVision files.
datasets.authors: Katarzyna Osowska, Julian Szymański, Witold Libionka

datasets.name: Intracranial EEG Epilepsy - Studies 3, 5 and 6 (Mayo Clinic; IEEG.org)
datasets.description: Long-term clinical intracranial EEG recordings from three patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, acquired at Mayo Clinic (Rochester, MN) using subdural grid/strip and depth electrodes. The dataset provides continuous multi-day recordings (about 397 hours across 41 runs) with expert seizure annotations. The recordings were originally shared via IEEG.org and Pennsieve Discover (Studies 3, 5 and 6) and are converted here to BIDS with lossless BrainVision encoding.
datasets.authors: Jenaye Johnson, Gregory Worrell, Brian Litt

datasets.name: Human subthalamic nucleus LFP and prefrontal subdural recordings during a working-memory encoding decision task - derivative
datasets.description: Derivative iEEG dataset of intraoperative recordings from 18 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation surgery. It contains macroelectrode local field potentials from STN trajectories and subdural prefrontal strip recordings acquired during a working-memory encoding task, in which participants viewed eight digits and remembered only those inside a target shape. Signals are band-passed, notch-filtered, downsampled to 1 kHz and re-referenced, then converted to BrainVision format with BIDS events.
datasets.authors: Baltazar A. Zavala, Anthony I. Jang, Kareem A. Zaghloul

datasets.name: iEEG networks preprocessing study (Shi, Pattnaik et al. 2024; HUP + MUSC): functional-connectivity networks for 2 re-referencing x 24 connectivity pipelines (derivative)
datasets.description: Derivative dataset of functional-connectivity networks computed from interictal intracranial EEG of 148 epilepsy patients at HUP and MUSC. For each 2-minute epoch it provides networks for two re-referencing schemes (common average and bipolar) crossed with 24 connectivity measures across frequency bands. It contains no time series. It repackages the Pennsieve release (doi:10.26275/4p8l-n5kt, creators Haoer Shi, Akash Pattnaik and Erin Conrad) accompanying the article 'Utility of intracranial EEG networks depends on re-referencing and connectivity choice' (Brain Communications 2024). The full article author list (Shi, Pattnaik, Aguila, Lucas, Sinha, Prager, Mojena, Gallagher, Parashos, Bonilha, Gleichgerrcht, Davis, Litt, Conrad) is credited in the Acknowledgements; the dataset creators listed here are those of the Pennsieve release.
datasets.authors: Haoer Shi, Akash Pattnaik, Erin Conrad

datasets.name: Network dynamics of HFOs (Lin & Stacey; Michigan): filtered and RMS iEEG snippets around interictal HFOs, 2 patients (derivative)
datasets.description: A derivative BIDS-iEEG repackaging of the Pennsieve dataset 'Network dynamics of HFOs'. It contains 80-500 Hz filtered signals and RMS envelopes of intracranial EEG snippets around interictal high frequency oscillations (HFOs), plus background snippets, from two epilepsy surgery patients with good and poor outcomes. Per-snippet HFO metadata, electrode coordinates, and seizure-onset-zone and resection masks are included to support HFO network dynamics analysis.
datasets.authors: Jack Lin, William C. Stacey

datasets.name: NeuroListen (Listening to the Brain): sEEG auditory-reconstruction features from 5 participants, authors' per-trial HGA/LFS/BBS arrays
datasets.description: This derivative dataset provides per-trial stereo-EEG (sEEG) feature arrays from five patients with epilepsy who passively listened to spoken Mandarin Chinese words, Mandarin digits and English words. Features include high-gamma activity, low-frequency signal and broadband representations at 200 Hz, computed after removal of epileptiform contacts and bipolar re-referencing. The data are repackaged from the authors' public release as epoched BrainVision files with events and stimulus audio and mel-spectrograms, supporting neural decoding and auditory reconstruction research.
datasets.authors: Xueyi Zhang, Ruicong Wang, Jialu Sun, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li

datasets.name: ECoG hemispheric asymmetry during reaching (Merrick et al. 2022): authors' 1000 Hz intracranial exports with reach kinematics
datasets.description: Intracranial electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six epilepsy patients with subdural grid implants, three in the left hemisphere and three in the right, performing an instructed-delay reaching task with each arm on a touchscreen. The dataset is a BIDS-packaged derivative of the authors' 1000 Hz exports, accompanied by reach kinematics. It supports study of hemispheric asymmetry in the encoding of bilateral arm kinematics in the human brain.
datasets.authors: Christina M. Merrick, Tanner C. Dixon, Assaf Breska, Jack J. Lin, Edward F. Chang, David King-Stephens, Kenneth D. Laxer, Peter B. Weber, Jose M. Carmena, Robert T. Knight, Richard B. Ivry

datasets.name: ECoG during a simple auditory reaction-time task, 8 subjects: stimulus-locked, response-locked and rest epochs at 400 Hz (Cho et al., physiological origin of ERPs)
datasets.description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from eight human subjects performing a simple auditory reaction-time task, in which they pressed a button as quickly as possible after an auditory stimulus. This derivative release provides downsampled (400 Hz) stimulus-locked, response-locked and rest epochs, repackaged in iEEG-BIDS from the authors' Zenodo deposit. The data support investigation of the physiological origin of event-related potentials.
datasets.authors: Hohyun Cho, Gerwin Schalk, Markus Adamek, Ladan Moheimanian, William G. Coon, Sung Chan Jun, Jonathan R. Wolpaw, Peter Brunner

datasets.name: Microelectrode recordings (MER) from deep brain stimulation surgery in Parkinson's disease (STN targeting, 14 patients)
datasets.description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings (MER) from 14 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing stereotactic deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery targeting the subthalamic nucleus. Up to three channels were recorded at successive depths along left and right trajectories. Depths are labelled as inside or outside the STN by neurophysiologists and surgeons. The data are unfiltered and were repackaged in iEEG-BIDS from a Zenodo release.
datasets.authors: Alfredo Rosado-Muñoz, Juan Francisco Guerrero-Martínez, Antonio Gutierrez Martín

datasets.name: Cortical and subthalamic brain recordings during hand-grip tasks in 16 patients with Parkinson’s disease
datasets.description: Intraoperative electrocorticography (ECoG) and subthalamic nucleus (STN) local field potential recordings from 16 patients with Parkinson's disease performing a grip-force task during bilateral DBS lead implantation. The dataset comprises 73 runs with subdural sensorimotor ECoG strips, four-contact STN DBS lead channels, and grip-force traces, with electrode locations localized in MNI space. Signals were resampled to 1 kHz and reorganized into BIDS from the original Harvard Dataverse release to support movement decoding research.
datasets.authors: Timon Merk, Victoria Peterson, Witold Lipski, Benjamin Blankertz, Robert S Turner, Ningfei Li, Andreas Horn, Robert Mark Richardson, Wolf-Julian Neumann

datasets.name: Brain-wide human sEEG during aversive eyepuffs and ketamine infusion (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025; DANDI 001347)
datasets.description: This dataset provides stereo-EEG (sEEG) recordings from seven adult epilepsy patients undergoing extended clinical monitoring at Stanford Hospital. Participants received brief aversive air puffs to the eye, and their responses were recorded before, during and after a 40-minute ketamine infusion (0.5 mg/kg). It is a BIDS-iEEG derivative of the NWB release on DANDI (001347), comprising 30 recordings at 200 Hz with contact labels and anatomical location labels but no electrode coordinates.
datasets.authors: Kauvar I, Richman EB, Liu TX, Li C, Vesuna S, Chibukhchyan A, Yamada L, Fogarty A, Solomon E, Choi EY, Mortazavi L, Chau Loo Kung G, Mukunda P, Raja C, Gil-Hernández D, Patron K, Zhang X, Brawer J, Wrobel S, Lusk Z, Lyu D, Mitra A, Hack L, Luo L, Grosenick L, van Roessel P, Williams LM, Heifets BD, Henderson JM, McNab JA, Rodríguez CI, Buch V, Nuyujukian P, Deisseroth K

datasets.name: Vanderbilt BIEN Lab Peri-ictal Dynamics Data (Makhoul et al. 2025): per-seizure SEEG partial directed coherence and imaginary coherence
datasets.description: This derivative BIDS-iEEG dataset provides per-seizure directed and undirected connectivity estimates, specifically partial directed coherence and imaginary coherence, computed from stereo-EEG recordings of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Connectivity is computed in sliding windows across peri-ictal periods and an interictal clip, in six frequency bands. Seizure-onset and propagation zone labels accompany each seizure. The release contains 78 patient folders and 994 connectivity files covering 708 seizure events, and no raw SEEG.
datasets.authors: Ghassan Makhoul, Kate Wang, Dario Englot

datasets.name: DRE-LZSH: SEEG benchmark dataset for drug-resistant epilepsy (ictal and interictal segments, 29 patients)
datasets.description: DRE-LZSH is a stereo-EEG (SEEG) benchmark dataset from 29 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, providing ictal (seizure) and interictal segments recorded at 2000 Hz. It includes clinical information, channel-level epileptogenic zone annotations, and the authors' derived results (HFO rates and 1/f spectral fits). The data were re-packaged losslessly into iEEG-BIDS from the original Zenodo release to support precision-medicine research on epileptogenic zone localization.
datasets.authors: Wang Yalin

datasets.name: Human-AI collaboration for co-managing epilepsy in real time: scalp EEG and SEEG from 13 epilepsy monitoring unit patients
datasets.description: This dataset contains continuous scalp EEG and stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings from 13 patients undergoing video-EEG monitoring in an epilepsy monitoring unit. It supports a prototype human-AI system in which a conversational smartphone agent collects patient and clinician feedback to retrain seizure detection models. The BIDS conversion includes per-recording-day EDF files, event annotations (seizures, patient events, sleep, medications), and derivative model outputs.
datasets.authors: Haoer Shi, Zack Goldblum, William Ojemann, Carlos Aguila, Kerry Nix, Katherine Walsh, Sarah Lavelle, Kathryn Davis, Nishant Sinha, Erin Conrad, Brian Litt

datasets.name: AIIsOutThere-2026-example
datasets.description: A stereo-EEG (sEEG) recording from one patient undergoing clinical intracranial monitoring, containing a single clinically confirmed seizure with bilateral tonic-clonic evolution. The recording comprises 100 sEEG contacts across 12 electrodes plus two marker inputs, sampled at 256 Hz for about 3.9 hours. Annotations mark the seizure and clinical onset. The data were originally shared on Zenodo and converted to iEEG-BIDS without signal processing.
datasets.authors: AI-is-out-there

datasets.name: s500-literature-164: Face-selective SEEG across the ventral occipito-temporal cortex in 140 participants, fast periodic visual stimulation (Jacques et al., 2025) (derivative)
datasets.description: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from 140 patients with refractory epilepsy undergoing presurgical evaluation, who viewed natural object images at 6 Hz with a face image every fifth item (1.2 Hz) in a fast periodic visual stimulation paradigm. The dataset covers 22,160 intracerebral contacts, most with Talairach coordinates and anatomical labels, sampling the ventral occipito-temporal cortex. It is a derivative release of the authors' minimally preprocessed Letswave data, repackaged in BIDS, and supports the study of concurrent category-selective activity in human visual recognition.
datasets.authors: Corentin Jacques, Jacques Jonas, Sophie Colnat-Coulbois, Bruno Rossion

datasets.name: s500-generic-45: Letter and word selective SEEG responses in the ventral occipito-temporal cortex, fast periodic visual stimulation (Lochy et al., 2018) (derivative)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings from 37 patients with refractory epilepsy viewing fast periodic visual stimulation, in which real words appeared at 2 Hz among pseudofonts, nonwords, or pseudowords presented at 10 Hz. The dataset probes letter- and word-selective responses in the ventral occipito-temporal cortex, measured at 2 Hz and its harmonics. This is a BIDS derivative of the authors' Letswave files, low-pass filtered at 40 Hz and cut into sequences, with electrode coordinates in Talairach and MNI spaces.
datasets.authors: Aliette Lochy, Corentin Jacques, Louis Maillard, Sophie Colnat-Coulbois, Bruno Rossion, Jacques Jonas

datasets.name: s500-literature-83: Example intracranial EEG with qHFO detections from 'Redaction of false High Frequency Oscillations due to muscle artifact' (Stacey lab, Mendeley Data)
datasets.description: An example intracranial EEG recording from one patient under intracranial monitoring, distributed with the code accompanying a study on redacting false high frequency oscillations (HFOs) caused by muscle artifact. It contains 61 channels sampled at 5000 Hz for 10 minutes, with 357 automated qHFO detections given as start/stop samples and channel. The recording demonstrates a wavelet-entropy feature that separates EMG-contaminated false HFOs from real HFOs.
datasets.authors: William Stacey, Stacey lab (University of Michigan)

datasets.name: VakilnaSEEG-fingerprint: sEEG seizure-onset and interictal segments of one polymicrogyria patient with electrode coordinates (Vakilna et al., 2025) (derivative)
datasets.description: Derivative sEEG dataset from a single patient with bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria and intractable focal seizures, comprising short sensor-space segments of seizure onset and interictal spikes. Data are provided in monopolar and bipolar montages as BrainVision files, with electrode coordinates for 228 located depth contacts. The data derive from a Brainstorm case study that used sLORETA source-space time-frequency fingerprint analysis to localize the epileptogenic zone, which was then treated with MR-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy.
datasets.authors: Vakilna, Yash Shashank, Atilgan, Deniz, Hampson, Johnson P, Chinara, Chinmay, Medani, Takfarinas, Leahy, Richard, Lacuey Lecumberri, Nuria, Lhatoo, Samden, Pati, Sandipan, Mosher, John, Gavvala, Jay

datasets.name: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings in human substantia nigra and globus pallidus during a social ultimatum game
datasets.description: Intraoperative single-unit microelectrode recordings from the human substantia nigra and globus pallidus in neurosurgical patients undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. Patients played a social ultimatum (exchange) game while wideband microelectrode and macro-contact signals were recorded, to study how these neurons encode social learning signals. The BIDS release contains 67 runs from 24 participants, with behavioral logs and task synchronisation events.
datasets.authors: Arianna Davis, Ofer Perl, Brian Kopell, Matthew Heflin, Salman Qasim, Zarghona Imtiaz, Ayaka Kato, Soojung Na, Navid Mikail, Helen S. Mayberg, P. Read Montague, Ignacio Saez, Xiaosi Gu

datasets.name: s500-generic-44: Crossmodal face-name person-identity frequency tagging, SEEG of the left ventral temporal cortex (Volfart et al., 2020) (derivative)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from the left ventral temporal cortex of three epilepsy patients (seven were tested, but four released files are empty) during crossmodal frequency-tagging stimulation. Faces and written names of a famous identity were presented at 4 Hz, with an identity change every 7th item (0.571 Hz), alongside face-only and name-only control conditions. This is a derivative repackaging of the authors' low-pass filtered Letswave sequences into BIDS iEEG format, with electrode coordinates in Talairach space.
datasets.authors: Angélique Volfart, Jacques Jonas, Louis Maillard, Sophie Colnat-Coulbois, Bruno Rossion

datasets.name: stim-seizures (Ojemann et al.; HUP + CHOP): seizure annotations, electrode localisations and preprocessed SEEG seizure traces (derivative)
datasets.description: A derivative BIDS-iEEG repackaging of the processed stim-seizures release from the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. It contains seizure annotations (clinician-marked and LSTM model-derived), electrode localisations, patient metadata, and four preprocessed bipolar SEEG seizure traces from patients who received 1 Hz low-frequency electrical stimulation. No raw iEEG recordings are included. The data support analyses of whether stimulation-induced seizures can replace spontaneous seizures and of seizure-generating networks.
datasets.authors: William K. Ojemann, Brian Litt, Erin Conrad

datasets.name: Spiking activity (MUA) and LFP from two microwires in human V2/V3, one patient, stimulus-locked epochs of 7 visual experiments (Self et al. 2016; derivative)
datasets.description: Stimulus-locked epochs of multi-unit activity (MUA), thresholded MUA, and local field potentials recorded from two microwires in human early visual cortex (V2/V3) of one epilepsy patient. The data cover seven visual experiments: receptive field mapping, orientation, spatial frequency, contrast and size tuning, contextual modulation, and curve tracing. It is a BIDS derivative repackaging of the Self et al. 2016 OSF release, with events annotated per epoch.
datasets.authors: Matthew W. Self, Judith C. Peters, Jessy K. Possel, Joel Reithler, Rainer Goebel, Peterjan Ris, Danique Jeurissen, Leila Reddy, Steven Claus, Johannes C. Baayen, Pieter R. Roelfsema

datasets.name: Intracranial recordings before and after left anterior temporal lobe disconnection during a speech prediction task (Kocsis et al., 2023) - derivative
datasets.description: Acute electrocorticography recordings from two epilepsy surgery patients at the University of Iowa, collected during a speech prediction task minutes before and after neurosurgical disconnection of the left anterior temporal lobe (a semantic hub). This derivative release provides 128-channel data at 1000 Hz, in downsampled and denoised (demodulated band transform plus first SVD component removal) versions. It also includes event codes and electrode localisation tables for studying the immediate neural impact of hub disconnection.
datasets.authors: Zsuzsanna Kocsis, Rick L. Jenison, Peter N. Taylor, Ryan M. Calmus, Bob McMurray, Ariane E. Rhone, McCall E. Sarrett, Carolina Deifelt Streese, Yukiko Kikuchi, Phillip E. Gander, Joel I. Berger, Christopher K. Kovach, Inyong Choi, Jeremy D. Greenlee, Hiroto Kawasaki, Thomas E. Cope, Timothy D. Griffiths, Matthew A. Howard III, Christopher I. Petkov

datasets.name: StarkweatherOFC-CCEP: orbitofrontal cortico-cortical evoked potential recordings, 7 patients (Starkweather et al.) (derivative)
datasets.description: Intracranial recordings of cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) elicited by single-pulse electrical stimulation of the orbitofrontal cortex in seven patients. The derivative release contains the authors' preprocessed per-electrode timeseries, unreferenced and bipolar, at 1000 Hz, along with stimulation event timings and amplitudes. It supports analysis of effective connectivity and rapid homotopic communication between orbitofrontal subregions.
datasets.authors: Clara Starkweather

datasets.name: s500-literature-201: Whole-night hippocampal depth and scalp Cz sleep EEG with spindle and ripple detections, 14 epilepsy patients (Ngo, Fell & Staresina, 2020) (derivative)
datasets.description: Whole-night sleep recordings from 14 pre-surgical epilepsy patients (135.6 h in total), with two channels per patient sampled at 1 kHz: a posterior hippocampal depth contact and scalp electrode Cz. The derivative dataset repackages the authors' OSF release into BIDS format and adds sleep stage scoring, artifact intervals, and automated sleep spindle and hippocampal ripple detections. It supports study of spindle-mediated hippocampal-neocortical coupling during sleep.
datasets.authors: Hong-Viet V. Ngo, Juergen Fell, Bernhard P. Staresina

datasets.name: s500-literature-171: Working-memory gating task iEEG, epoched bipolar ECoG/sEEG from 11 patients with Yeo-7 network labels (Johnson et al., 2023) (derivative)
datasets.description: Preprocessed, bipolar-referenced intracranial EEG (ECoG/sEEG) from 11 neurosurgical epilepsy patients performing a single-trial working-memory gating task with context-first and context-last conditions. The derivative release contains the authors' epoched, filtered and artifact-cleaned trials, with trial-level behavioral information, electrode positions and Yeo-7 network labels. It supports investigation of theta network mechanisms of flexible information encoding and input gating in prefrontal cortex.
datasets.authors: Elizabeth L. Johnson, Jack J. Lin, David King-Stephens, Peter B. Weber, Kenneth D. Laxer, Ignacio Saez, Fady Girgis, Mark D'Esposito, Robert T. Knight, David Badre

datasets.name: Hoy2024 effort decision LFP: subthalamic/pallidal and prefrontal recordings during an effort-based decision task (DBS surgery)
datasets.description: Intraoperative local field potential recordings from the subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus and from prefrontal cortex (frontopolar or orbitofrontal) in five patients undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery while performing an effort-based decision-making task. The derivative BIDS release includes the authors' preprocessed, epoched bipolar signals with trial-level behavioural and model variables, as well as continuous raw neural exports. It supports analysis of beta and theta oscillations related to effort and previous reward during decision making.
datasets.authors: Colin W. Hoy, Coralie de Hemptinne, Sarah S. Wang, Catherine J. Harmer, Matthew A. J. Apps, Masud Husain, Philip A. Starr, Simon Little

datasets.name: Qin2023 action observation ECoG: re-referenced region-of-interest electrocorticography during observation of predictable and unpredictable action movies
datasets.description: Continuous electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded at 1000 Hz from 10 epilepsy patients (8.7 hours in total) while they watched movies of sequential actions that were either predictable or unpredictable. The dataset contains re-referenced region-of-interest channels, camera-change event tables, electrode positions in ACPC and MNI space, and the stimulus movies with annotations. It is a BIDS derivative repackaging of the authors' OSF release, supporting analysis of predictive coding and information flow during action observation.
datasets.authors: Chaoyi Qin, Frederic Michon, Yoshiyuki Onuki, Yohei Ishishita, Keisuke Otani, Kensuke Kawai, Pascal Fries, Valeria Gazzola, Christian Keysers

datasets.name: Treder2021 hippocampal switchboard: epoched intracranial EEG during object/scene localiser and associative recall (extra-hippocampal channels)
datasets.description: Epoched intracranial EEG from 11 epilepsy patients (22 recordings, about 9 hours of epochs at 200 Hz) recorded during an object/scene localiser task and an associative recall task. The data are the extra-hippocampal channels released by Treder et al. (2021) on OSF and repackaged into BIDS iEEG format. The original study examined the role of the hippocampus as a switchboard between perception and memory.
datasets.authors: Matthias S. Treder, Ian Charest, Sebastian Michelmann, María Carmen Martín-Buro, Frédéric Roux, Fernando Carceller-Benito, Arturo Ugalde-Canitrot, David T. Rollings, Vijay Sawlani, Ramesh Chelvarajah, Maria Wimber, Simon Hanslmayr, Bernhard P. Staresina

datasets.name: Xie2026 amygdala ablation PTSD: epoched stereo-EEG of the index patient before and after right amygdala radiofrequency ablation (interpretation-bias task)
datasets.description: Epoched stereo-EEG recordings (157 contacts, 200 Hz, 588 trials) from a single patient with post-traumatic stress disorder performing a face interpretation-bias task. Data were recorded before and after SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation of the right amygdala. The dataset repackages the authors' OSF release into BIDS derivative format with per-contact anatomical labels and coordinates.
datasets.authors: Tao Xie, Sanne J. H. van Rooij, Sai Sun, Noah K. Bryson, Phillip Demarest, Haeorum Park, Luigi Maccotta, Shuo Wang, Peter Brunner, Jon T. Willie

datasets.name: Intraoperative STN/thalamic DBS-lead LFP with subgaleal sensorimotor strips during a stop-signal task (Diesburg, Greenlee & Wessel, 2021)
datasets.description: Intraoperative local field potentials recorded during deep brain stimulation surgery from DBS leads in the subthalamic nucleus or ventral intermediate thalamus, together with subgaleal electrode strips over sensorimotor cortex. Twenty-three patients performed an auditory stop-signal task and a go-only localizer. The data support analysis of cortico-subcortical beta burst dynamics underlying movement cancellation, in which subcortical beta bursts on successful stop trials are followed within about 50 ms by sensorimotor cortical beta bursts.
datasets.authors: Darcy A. Diesburg, Jeremy D. W. Greenlee, Jan R. Wessel

datasets.name: The neural activity of auditory conscious perception: intracranial EEG epochs (Christison-Lagay et al. 2025; derivative: authors' 2-s grey-matter epochs)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset provides epoched, artifact-screened intracranial EEG from adults with drug-resistant epilepsy performing an auditory perceptual threshold task. A 75 ms target sound was embedded in white noise at each participant's 50% detection threshold, and trials are sorted into Perceived, Not Perceived and blank categories. The release contains 2-second grey-matter electrode epochs from 30 participants (32 recordings), repackaged from the authors' Dryad deposit into BIDS. Continuous recordings were not released. The position of the target sound within each 2-s epoch is not stated in the release, so epoch timing relative to the stimulus should be treated as unknown.
datasets.authors: Kate L. Christison-Lagay, Aya Khalaf, Noah C. Freedman, Christopher Micek, Sharif I. Kronemer, Mariana M. Gusso, Lauren Kim, Sarit Forman, Julia Ding, Mark Aksen, Ahmad Abdel-Aty, Hunki Kwon, Noah Markowitz, Erin Yeagle, Elizabeth Espinal, Jose Herrero, Stephan Bickel, James Young, Ashesh Mehta, Kun Wu, Jason Gerrard, Eyiyemisi Damisah, Dennis Spencer, Jiayin Qu, Hal Blumenfeld

datasets.name: ECoG_HB_02: hybrid-density ECoG high-gamma features with synchronised speech, one participant (derivative)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset repackages the publicly released single-participant ECoG record (ECoG_HB_02) from Chen et al. 2024. It contains 125 Hz high-gamma (70-150 Hz) envelope features recorded with a hybrid-density grid, together with synchronised speech audio and word-level trial events. The raw ECoG voltages were not released; the data are provided as BrainVision float32 with the original HB02.h5 file preserved in sourcedata.
datasets.authors: Xupeng Chen

datasets.name: STN local field potentials from awake Parkinson's disease patients ON and OFF medication, with and without DBS (Wiest et al. 2023)
datasets.description: Subthalamic nucleus (STN) local field potentials recorded together with scalp EEG and accelerometers from patients with Parkinson's disease 3-6 days after DBS surgery, while the leads were externalised. Recordings were made OFF and ON dopaminergic medication, at rest and during 130 Hz STN stimulation sessions. The data underlie an analysis showing that the aperiodic exponent of STN field potentials increases with levodopa and with DBS.
datasets.authors: Christoph Wiest, Flavie Torrecillos, Alek Pogosyan, Fahd Baig, Erlick A. Pereira, Francesca Morgante, Keyoumars Ashkan, Huiling Tan

datasets.name: Subthalamic and thalamic local field potentials during DBS in cervical dystonia, DC-removed derivative at 4096 Hz
datasets.description: Local field potentials recorded from externalised octopolar DBS leads in 7 patients with isolated cervical dystonia (12 hemispheres), spanning the subthalamic nucleus, rostral zona incerta and ventrolateral thalamus. Recordings were made 4-7 days after surgery, off medication, during DBS ramps and single-pulse stimulation, with scalp EEG, neck EMG and accelerometry in some patients. This derivative release at 4096 Hz has DC offset removed and is repackaged in BIDS (BrainVision) from the original Oxford deposit.
datasets.authors: Christoph Wiest, Flavie Torrecillos, Francesca Morgante, Erlick Pereira, Huiling Tan

datasets.name: Intraoperative VIM thalamus microelectrode recordings during transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS) for essential tremor (Luu et al.; derivative: authors' processed 48 kHz signals)
datasets.description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the ventral intermediate (VIM) thalamus of 9 adults with medication-refractory essential tremor undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. At each recording depth, 60 s were recorded with and without transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS), a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation therapy applied to the treated hand. This derivative dataset repackages the authors' processed 48 kHz signals into BIDS (BrainVision float32) with depth, stimulation settings and motion-artifact masks.
datasets.authors: Cuong P. Luu, Jordan Ranum, Youngwon Youn, Jennifer L. Perrault, Bryan M. Krause, Matthew I. Banks, Laura Buyan-Dent, Kip A. Ludwig, Wendell B. Lake, Aaron J. Suminski

datasets.name: A multimodal epilepsy dataset of paired 3-Tesla and 7-Tesla MRI and intracranial EEG (Penn 3T-7T, Pennsieve 662)
datasets.description: This dataset provides paired 3-Tesla and 7-Tesla MRI (structural and resting-state fMRI) from 30 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. For 15 of these patients it also includes curated ictal and interictal intracranial EEG epochs, with electrode localization from iEEG-recon. Derivatives from fMRIPrep, FreeSurfer and iEEG-recon are included. The data are a BIDS redistribution of Pennsieve Discover dataset 662.
datasets.authors: Alfredo Lucas, Mariam Josyula, Nina Petillo, Joost Wagenaar, Joel Stein, Sandhitsu Das, Nishant Sinha, Kathryn Davis, Tamjid Imtiaz

datasets.name: Human medial temporal lobe iEEG during a visual working memory task (Boran et al.; DANDI 000575)
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG recordings from depth electrodes in the medial temporal lobe (amygdala, hippocampus, entorhinal and parahippocampal cortex) of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a visual working memory change-detection task. Set sizes of 1, 2, 4 or 6 coloured squares were memorised, retained over a delay and compared with a test array. This BIDS-iEEG representation converts the continuous series from the authors' NWB release on DANDI (000575), covering 11 participants and 13 recordings.
datasets.authors: Ece Boran, Peter Hilfiker, Lennart Stieglitz, Jan Hohenheim, Peter Klaver, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: Klocke-2024-supraspinal-10.1093/brain/awae223
datasets.description: This dataset contains multimodal recordings from 12 patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease and bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. Subthalamic local field potentials were recorded with a Medtronic Percept PC, together with 48-channel scalp EEG, surface EMG and APDM inertial sensor data. Recordings were made during sitting, standing and several walking tasks, including walking with stops and a dual task, after overnight medication withdrawal with stimulation off. The data support investigation of supraspinal mechanisms of gait impairment and freezing of gait.
datasets.authors: Philipp Klocke, Moritz Loeffler, Daniel Weiss

datasets.name: Dareplane proof of concept: STN LFP, ECoG and EOG during the CopyDraw task with open- and closed-loop DBS (1 Parkinson's disease patient)
datasets.description: Intracranial recordings from one Parkinson's disease patient with externalised bilateral subthalamic DBS leads and an epidural ECoG strip over left primary motor cortex. Data were acquired on days 2-4 after implantation while the patient performed the CopyDraw task with DBS off, with continuous open-loop DBS, and with closed-loop adaptive DBS run on the Dareplane platform. The dataset serves as a proof of concept for the Dareplane modular open-source BCI software platform and includes STN LFP, ECoG, EOG and stimulation/port event markers.
datasets.authors: Matthias Dold, Joana Pereira, Bastian Sajonz, Volker A. Coenen, Jordy Thielen, Marcus L.F. Janssen, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: Developmental ECoG: resting-state electrocorticography from 13 epilepsy patients aged 3-33 years
datasets.description: Resting-state intracranial electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from 13 patients with epilepsy aged 3.4-33.9 years, collected during clinical monitoring at Seattle Children's Hospital and Harborview Medical Center. Recordings come from subdural grids and strips. Some participants also had depth electrodes, but the sub-02 depth channels are not part of the deposited recording. The data were used to study developmental relationships between the alpha rhythm and intrinsic neural timescales. They are re-packaged in iEEG-BIDS without signal processing.
datasets.authors: Jesse T. Miles, Kurt E. Weaver, Sara Jane Webb, Jeffrey G. Ojemann

datasets.name: Wakeful and sleep-like states in subdural ECoG (Pahwa et al., 2015): 4 patients, 64-channel grids
datasets.description: Subdural electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from four patients with intractable epilepsy, implanted with 8x8 grids over left frontal, temporal and parietal cortex during clinical monitoring. For each patient, two wakeful and two sleep-like epochs were identified from video and audio of natural behaviour, without any task. The dataset supports work on detecting wakeful and sleep-like states for future ECoG brain-computer interface applications.
datasets.authors: Mrinal Pahwa, Matthew Kusner, Carl D. Hacker, David T. Bundy, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Eric C. Leuthardt

datasets.name: Face-selective ventral occipito-temporal responses to fast periodic visual stimulation, SEEG (Jonas et al., 2016) (derivative)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from 28 patients with refractory epilepsy during fast periodic visual stimulation. Natural object images were presented at 6 Hz, with faces appearing every fifth image (1.2 Hz) in the periodic condition and at random positions in the non-periodic control condition. This derivative release repackages the authors' Letswave files, which were low-pass filtered at 30 Hz and segmented into sequences. It supports mapping of face-selective responses across the ventral occipito-temporal cortex.
datasets.authors: Jacques Jonas, Corentin Jacques, Joan Liu-Shuang, Hélène Brissart, Sophie Colnat-Coulbois, Louis Maillard, Bruno Rossion

datasets.name: Subthalamic local field potentials during the balloon analogue risk task (Pearson et al., 2017): Parkinson's disease DBS surgery (derivative: decimated LFP)
datasets.description: Intraoperative subthalamic nucleus local field potential recordings from patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing deep brain stimulation implantation while performing a self-paced balloon analogue risk task. The derivative release repackages decimated LFP (200 Hz, with a few 250 Hz recordings) from 14 patients as BIDS iEEG, with behavioural trial events and artifact-censoring intervals. It supports investigation of neural activity preceding impulsive and risky choices.
datasets.authors: John M. Pearson, Patrick T. Hickey, Shivanand P. Lad, Michael L. Platt, Dennis A. Turner

datasets.name: Thalamic local field potentials during reading aloud of words and nonwords (Wang et al., 2022): 11 essential tremor patients, DBS surgery (derivative: preprocessed epochs)
datasets.description: Preprocessed, epoched local field potentials from the ventral lateral thalamus of 11 essential tremor patients, recorded during awake deep brain stimulation (DBS) lead implantation while they read aloud consonant-vowel-consonant words and nonwords. Recordings come from mapping-electrode macroelectrode rings in 4 patients and implanted DBS leads in 7 patients. This derivative repackages the authors' Dryad release, with non-re-referenced trials stored as BrainVision segments, trial tables as events, and MNI contact coordinates as electrodes.
datasets.authors: Dengyu Wang, Witold J. Lipski, Alan Bush, Anna Chrabaszcz, Christina Dastolfo-Hromack, Michael W. Dickey, Julie A. Fiez, R. Mark Richardson

datasets.name: Executed and imagined grasp forces recorded with stereo-EEG (Murphy et al., 2016): 4 participants, power and pinch force-matching
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from four adults with drug-resistant epilepsy performing force-matching tasks with power grasp and lateral pinch. Two participants also completed blocks in which they only imagined producing the force. Each block contained trials at three force targets (20, 30 and 40% of maximum voluntary contraction). The recordings were sampled at 2000 Hz together with an analog dynamometer signal, and are provided in BIDS format with force-target events.
datasets.authors: Brian A. Murphy, Jonathan P. Miller, Kabilar Gunalan, A. Bolu Ajiboye

datasets.name: Brain criticality predicts individual levels of inter-areal synchronization (Fusca, Siebenhuehner, Wang et al., 2023): SEEG/MEG PLV and DFA (derivative)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset repackages the authors' public Dryad release of phase-synchronization and detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) results from resting-state SEEG in 68 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients and MEG in 52 healthy participants. It includes per-patient complex phase-locking value matrices, DFA exponents, and epileptogenic-zone contact masks, as well as group-level MEG wPLI/DFA data and Kuramoto-model simulations. The data support the finding that brain criticality predicts individual levels of inter-areal synchronization. Raw recordings are not included.
datasets.authors: Felix Siebenhühner, Marco Fuscà, Sheng Hua Wang, Vladislav Myrov, Gabriele Arnulfo, Lino Nobili, J Matias Palva, Satu Palva

datasets.name: Human ECoG speaking consonant-vowel syllables
datasets.description: High-density (256-channel) electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded at the University of California, San Francisco, from epilepsy patients reading aloud consonant-vowel syllables. The dataset includes 31 recording blocks from four subject codes, with hand-marked annotations of syllable onset, consonant-vowel transition and offset, plus rest baselines and anatomical electrode labels. It supports study of the functional organization of human ventral sensorimotor cortex during speech articulation and is organized as iEEG-BIDS with the original NWB files.
datasets.authors: Kristofer E. Bouchard, Edward F Chang, Ben Dichter

datasets.name: Vanderbilt BIEN Lab SOZ Resting State SEEG Classification (processed resting-state SEEG)
datasets.description: Processed resting-state stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from 79 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy evaluated at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Each patient contributed five minutes of awake, eyes-closed interictal data, band-pass filtered and stored in a bipolar montage, with region-level seizure onset zone labels based on Desikan-Killiany parcellation. The dataset supports deep learning classification of seizure onset zone versus non-seizure onset zone brain regions.
datasets.authors: Kate Wang, Sameer Sundrani, Dario Englot

datasets.name: Motor imagination and execution with a chronic wireless epidural ECoG BCI (WIMAGINE), one participant with tetraplegia (Pollina et al. 2026)
datasets.description: Epidural ECoG recordings from one participant with incomplete tetraplegia (C6 spinal cord injury) implanted with the wireless WIMAGINE device over left primary motor and sensory cortex. The participant executed or imagined right-arm reaching and wrist-extension movements, singly or simultaneously (one executed and one imagined), across eight sessions. The derivative release contains 1-250 Hz band-pass filtered signals from 32 channels, with events and EMG-related source data, repackaged in iEEG-BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Leonardo Pollina, Lucas Struber, Valeria De Seta, Eleonora Russo, Serpil Karakas, Stephan Chabardes, Tetiana Aksenova, Guillaume Charvet, Solaiman Shokur, Silvestro Micera

datasets.name: Internal-external attention switching SEEG epochs, DMN and DAN channels, 25 epilepsy patients (Hammer et al. 2024)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG epochs from 25 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a task that alternated between external attention (visual search) and internal attention (questions about personal experiences). Epochs span -4 to +4 s around each task switch and include only bipolar channels assigned to the default mode network and dorsal attention network (Yeo-7 atlas). The data are the authors' preprocessed epochs, repackaged in iEEG-BIDS format as a derivative dataset.
datasets.authors: Jiri Hammer

datasets.name: Multi-Expert Seizure Annotation
datasets.description: Stereotactic EEG recordings of 78 seizures (44 spontaneous, 34 stimulation-induced) from 29 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, recruited at the University of Pennsylvania and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Three or five board-certified epileptologists independently annotated each seizure for onset time, onset channels, and channels seizing 10 seconds after onset using a standardized protocol. The BIDS-formatted data include electrode localizations, patient demographics, and clinical outcomes, and serve as a benchmark for validating automated seizure onset and spread detection against expert consensus.
datasets.authors: William K. Ojemann, Daniel Zhou, Caren Armstrong, Nishant Sinha, Brian Litt, Erin Conrad

datasets.name: Genuine cross-frequency coupling networks in human resting-state electrophysiological recordings (Siebenhuehner et al., 2020): SEEG and MEG connectomes (derivative)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset repackages the public Dryad release of Siebenhühner et al. (2020), providing per-subject resting-state connectivity matrices computed from stereo-EEG (59 epilepsy patients) and MEG (19 healthy participants plus a 10-participant eyes-open/eyes-closed cohort). Measures include phase synchrony (PLV, wPLI), cross-frequency phase synchrony, phase-amplitude coupling and amplitude-envelope coupling, each with surrogate values. Supporting files, neuropsychological scores and plotted figure values are also included. Raw recordings are not available because of data privacy regulations.
datasets.authors: Felix Siebenhühner, Sheng H Wang, Gabriele Arnulfo, Lino Nobili, J Matias Palva, Satu Palva, Anna Lampinen

datasets.name: Ripples reflect a spectrum of synchronous spiking activity in human anterior temporal lobe (Tong et al., 2021): figure-level iEEG, micro-LFP and spiking arrays (derivative)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset repackages figure-level arrays from Tong et al. (2021), which examined hippocampal-adjacent anterior temporal lobe ripples in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a paired-associates verbal memory task. It contains ripple-band signals, time-frequency power, ripple rasters, micro-LFP and spike data from subdural/depth iEEG contacts and 96-channel Utah microelectrode arrays, covering 7 participants and the panels of Figures 1-4. Raw continuous recordings are not included. Session date strings were removed for privacy.
datasets.authors: Ai Phuong Tong, Alex Vaz, John Wittig, Sara Inati, Kareem Zaghloul

datasets.name: iEEG during direct electrical stimulation of orbitofrontal and other sites (Rao, Sellers et al., 2018): continuous-stimulation and single-pulse recordings
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (ECoG grids/strips and depth/stereo-EEG electrodes) from 17 adults undergoing inpatient seizure monitoring, recorded before, during and after continuous 100 Hz direct electrical stimulation of the lateral orbitofrontal cortex and other sites, as well as during single-pulse electrical stimulation. The data accompany a study showing that unilateral lateral OFC stimulation acutely improved mood in participants with moderate-to-severe baseline depression symptoms and suppressed low-frequency OFC power. Mood assessments and clinical metadata are included, converted to iEEG-BIDS.
datasets.authors: Vikram Rao, Kristin Sellers, Deanna Wallace, Morgan Lee, Maryam Bijanzadeh, Omid Sani, Yuxiao Yang, Maryam Shanechi, Heather Dawes, Edward Chang

datasets.name: Rapid coordination of effective learning by the human hippocampus: intracranial EEG during scene recognition with eye tracking
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from six patients with medically refractory epilepsy performing a scene recognition memory task with concurrent EyeLink eye tracking. The dataset investigates how the human hippocampus rapidly coordinates effective learning during study and gaze-contingent recognition testing of natural scenes. It is a lossless iEEG-BIDS re-packaging of the authors' public Zenodo release, with electrode MNI coordinates and source data included.
datasets.authors: James E. Kragel, Stephan Schuele, Stephen VanHaerents, Joshua M. Rosenow, Joel L. Voss

datasets.name: Human Responses to Visually Evoked Threat: intracranial EEG during virtual-reality heights, no-heights and shark stimuli (3 patients)
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG recordings from three patients with treatment-resistant epilepsy who viewed immersive virtual-reality stimuli: a virtual-heights scene, a no-heights baseline, and (in two patients) a 360-degree great white shark movie. Skin conductance and visual-scanning measures were collected alongside the iEEG, with electrode coverage in the insula and orbitofrontal cortex. The raw TDT exports are repackaged in BIDS (BrainVision format) without signal processing.
datasets.authors: Melis Yilmaz Balban, Erin Cafaro, Lauren Saue-Fletcher, Marlon Joseph Washington, Maryam Bijanzadeh, Andrew Moses Lee, Edward Chang, Andrew Huberman

datasets.name: Intracranial EEG from 9 adults during a memory-guided actions experiment (preprocessed epochs, Moraresku et al.)
datasets.description: Preprocessed stereo-EEG epochs from nine patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a delayed memory-guided action task at the Motol Epilepsy Center in Prague. The derivative dataset contains bipolar-referenced, notch-filtered and downsampled epochs time-locked to encoding onset, with trial information, channel rejection labels and MNI electrode coordinates. It supports investigation of interactions between dorsal and ventral visual streams and the hippocampus during working memory and action.
datasets.authors: Sofiia Moraresku, Jiri Hammer, Vasileios Dimakopoulos, Michaela Kajsova, Radek Janca, Petr Jezdik, Adam Kalina, Petr Marusic, Kamil Vlcek

datasets.name: Neural interactions in the human frontal cortex dissociate reward and punishment learning (Combrisson et al., 2024): preprocessed SEEG high-gamma power, 16 patients (derivative)
datasets.description: Preprocessed high-gamma power (50-100 Hz) from stereotactic EEG recordings in 16 patients with pharmaco-resistant epilepsy performing a probabilistic instrumental learning task with reward and punishment conditions. The derivative dataset contains 248 bipolar derivations in the anterior insula, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, lateral orbitofrontal cortex and ventromedial prefrontal cortex, time-locked to outcome. It supports information-theoretic analyses of how frontal regions form separate reward and punishment subsystems that interact when encoding prediction errors.
datasets.authors: Etienne Combrisson, Ruggero Basanisi, Sylvain Rheims, Philippe Kahane, Julien Bastin, Andrea Brovelli

datasets.name: Intracranial entrainment reveals statistical learning across levels of abstraction (Sherman et al., 2023): raw iEEG from 8 neurosurgical patients
datasets.description: Raw intracranial EEG (iEEG) recorded from 8 neurosurgical patients with epilepsy while they viewed rapid streams of scene photographs containing statistical regularities at the category or exemplar level. Neural entrainment (phase coherence) at the image frequency (2 Hz) and the pair frequency (1 Hz) was used to track online statistical learning across levels of abstraction. The data are converted to iEEG-BIDS without signal modification, with electrode coordinates in MNI space.
datasets.authors: Brynn Sherman, Ayman Aljishi, Kathryn Graves, Imran Quraishi, Adithya Sivaraju, Eyiyemisi Damisah, Nicholas Turk-Browne

datasets.name: Autoscopic hallucinations elicited by stimulation of periventricular nodular heterotopia (SEEG, 1 patient)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from one drug-resistant epilepsy patient with a right posterior temporal periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH). High-frequency (43 Hz) electrical stimulation of the PVNH elicited autoscopic hallucinations, and single-pulse electrical stimulation was used to map effective connectivity. The dataset includes 4096 Hz iEEG recordings, stimulation event markers, contact coordinates and a defaced T1 image, supporting multi-modal connectivity analysis of the network underlying bodily self-consciousness.
datasets.authors: Flavius Ionut Bratu, Irina Oane, Andrei Barborica, Cristian Donos, Constantin Pistol, Andrei Daneasa, Camelia Lentoiu, Ioana Mindruta

datasets.name: Sensorimotor alpha and beta ECoG during movement imagery (Stolk et al. 2019, shared participants S4-S6)
datasets.description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from three epilepsy patients (S4-S6) who imagined grasping a tilted cylinder with the left or right hand. The data are the subset of participants from Stolk et al. (2019) who consented to data sharing, released as epoched trial segments with electrode positions. The dataset supports study of alpha and beta rhythmic activity in the human sensorimotor cortex during motor imagery.
datasets.authors: Arjen Stolk, Loek Brinkman, Mariska J. Vansteensel, Erik Aarnoutse, Frans S.S. Leijten, Chris H. Dijkerman, Robert T. Knight, Floris P. de Lange, Ivan Toni

datasets.name: Human medial temporal lobe single units during a verbal working memory task (Boran et al.): spike times and waveforms aligned to OpenNeuro ds004752
datasets.description: This BIDS derivative dataset provides single-unit (microwire) recordings from the medial temporal lobe of nine patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy performing a modified Sternberg verbal working memory task. It contains 1526 sorted units from the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex and amygdala, with spike times per trial, mean and standard deviation waveforms, unit-to-electrode anatomical mapping, and trial properties. Subject, session and trial labels are aligned to OpenNeuro ds004752 (NEMAR on004752), which holds the matching scalp and intracranial EEG. The data originate from the Boran et al. release and were re-packaged without changing values.
datasets.authors: Ece Boran, Tommaso Fedele, Adrian Steiner, Peter Hilfiker, Lennart Stieglitz, Thomas Grunwald, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: MNI Open iEEG Atlas: normal intracranial EEG in wakefulness and sleep (processed 200 Hz atlas clips)
datasets.description: The MNI Open iEEG Atlas (processed 200 Hz clips) provides normal intracranial EEG from 106 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, recorded at three tertiary epilepsy centres. It contains one minute of artifact-free bipolar sEEG/ECoG per vigilance state (wakefulness, N2, N3, REM) plus up to 10 minutes of N2 and N3 sleep, restricted to channels judged to record normal activity. The data were filtered, resampled to 200 Hz and cleaned by the source authors, and are deposited as a BIDS derivative with channel coordinates in MNI space.
datasets.authors: Birgit Frauscher, Nicolás von Ellenrieder, Rina Zelmann, Irena Doležalová, Lorella Minotti, André Olivier, Jeffery Hall, Dominique Hoffmann, Dang Khoa Nguyen, Philippe Kahane, François Dubeau, Jean Gotman, Christine Rogers

datasets.name: Annotated interictal epileptiform discharges in intracranial EEG (iEEG) sleep data (Falach et al., 2024)
datasets.description: This dataset contains multichannel intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 25 epilepsy patients during overnight sleep, acquired at two medical centers (Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center and UCLA). It includes 852 interictal epileptiform discharges, mainly from the medial temporal lobe, annotated by expert neurologists. The data are organized in BIDS format with electrode coordinates, sleep scoring, and clinical metadata to support development of automated IED detection methods.
datasets.authors: Rotem Falach, Maya Geva-Sagiv, Dawn Eliashiv, Lilach Goldstein, Ofer Budin, Guy Gurevitch, Genela Morris, Ido Strauss, Amir Globerson, Firas Fahoum, Itzhak Fried, Yuval Nir

datasets.name: Stolk et al. 2018 FieldTrip iEEG protocol dataset (SubjectUCI29): authors' preprocessed ECoG+SEEG epochs
datasets.description: Preprocessed intracranial EEG (ECoG and SEEG) from one epilepsy patient (SubjectUCI29) released with the FieldTrip human intracranial analysis protocol of Stolk et al. (2018). The data comprise 26 epochs of 152 channels sampled at 5000 Hz, aligned to target-tone onset in an auditory detection task with a button-press response. The epochs were demeaned, low-pass filtered and band-stop filtered by the original authors. The raw recordings were not shared, so the dataset is packaged as a BIDS derivative together with electrode coordinates.
datasets.authors: Arjen Stolk, Sandon Griffin, Roemer van der Meij, Callum Dewar, Ignacio Saez, Jack J. Lin, Giovanni Piantoni, Jan-Mathijs Schoffelen, Robert T. Knight, Robert Oostenveld

datasets.name: Arithmetic calculations measured by intracranial EEG in the human brain
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from 20 pharmacoresistant epilepsy patients undergoing presurgical evaluation while they solved sequential three-operand arithmetic equations (easy and difficult, in several symbolic formats). The deposit contains preprocessed, bipolar-referenced epochs (-2 to +7 s around the first operand, 512 Hz) with MNI coordinates of the contact pairs. It supports analyses of the temporal order of activations and interactions in the brain during arithmetic calculation.
datasets.authors: M. Kalinova, B. Kerkova, A. Kalina, V. Pytelova, J. Amlerova, R. Janca, P. Jezdik, D. Krysl, M. Kudr, P. Krsek, P. Marusic, J. Hammer

datasets.name: Bern-Barcelona EEG database: focal and nonfocal intracranial EEG signal pairs (Andrzejak, Schindler & Rummel 2012)
datasets.description: The Bern-Barcelona EEG database contains 7500 pairs of intracranial EEG signals, 3750 focal and 3750 non-focal, drawn from five patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy. Each pair is a 20-second segment sampled at 512 Hz and recorded during seizure-free intervals. The dataset supports nonlinear time series analysis of focal versus non-focal activity. This BIDS version is a lossless repackaging of the published source text files, with patient, channel and time of origin not recorded.
datasets.authors: Ralph G. Andrzejak, Kaspar Schindler, Christian Rummel

datasets.name: Bonn intracranial EEG segments, sets C, D and E (Andrzejak et al. 2001)
datasets.description: This dataset contains 300 single-channel intracranial EEG segments (23.6 s each, 173.61 Hz) from five epilepsy patients undergoing presurgical evaluation at the University of Bonn. It comprises sets C and D (seizure-free interval recordings from the opposite hippocampal formation and the epileptogenic zone) and set E (ictal activity), repackaged losslessly in iEEG-BIDS from the original Andrzejak et al. (2001) release. The segments were originally used to study nonlinear deterministic and finite-dimensional structure in brain electrical activity as a function of recording region and brain state.
datasets.authors: Ralph G. Andrzejak, Klaus Lehnertz, Florian Mormann, Christoph Rieke, Peter David, Christian E. Elger

datasets.name: IEEG004: A library of human electrocorticographic data and analyses (Kai J. Miller) - calibrated task subset
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted subset of Kai Miller's library of human electrocorticographic (ECoG) data, covering six calibrated tasks: finger flexion, hand gestures, motor imagery, basic motor movement, and speech (verb generation and noun reading). It contains 111 recordings from 24 epilepsy patients with subdural electrode grids, recorded at 1 kHz at Harborview Hospital. The data are scaled to physical units and include events, channel metadata and electrode positions.
datasets.authors: Kai J. Miller

datasets.name: Chamanzar2020: Ultra high-density EEG of interictal migraine and controls during visual, auditory stimulation and rest
datasets.description: Ultra high-density 128-channel EEG recorded from 18 individuals with migraine (interictal) and 21 healthy controls. Recordings include steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) and steady-state auditory evoked potential (SSAEP) tasks at 4 and 6 Hz, as well as eyes-open resting state. The data support analyses of cortical coherence abnormalities in migraine.
datasets.authors: Alireza Chamanzar, Sarah M. Haigh, Pulkit Grover, Marlene Behrmann
datasets.eeg_reference: BioSemi CMS/DRL (online); no offline reference applied
datasets.placement_scheme: Custom ultra-high-density layout (~14 mm centre-to-centre) over occipital, parietal and frontal areas; channel labels follow 10-5 names but positions are custom (Chamanzar et al. 2021, Fig. 2). No digitized positions were released.

datasets.name: Perdikis2018: CNBI EPFL Cybathlon BCI-race motor-imagery dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from two tetraplegic pilots of team Brain Tweakers (CNBI, EPFL) during longitudinal motor-imagery BCI training for the Cybathlon 2016 BCI race. The dataset contains 16-channel EEG from cue-based offline calibration runs with three classes (both hands, both feet, rest), recorded at 512 Hz. It was re-released in BIDS format from the original Zenodo deposit via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Serafeim Perdikis, Luca Tonin, Sareh Saeedi, Christoph Schneider, Jose del R. Millan

datasets.name: Farabbi2020: Motor-Imagery EEG dataset during robot-arm control
datasets.description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing cued left- versus right-hand imagery to control a Baxter robot arm reaching toward objects. Each participant completed three sessions with first-person and third-person visual feedback conditions, giving 480 trials per subject. Data were recorded with a 32-channel LiveAmp system at 250 Hz and re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Andrea Farabbi, Fabiola Ghiringhelli, Luca Mainardi, Joao Miguel Sanches, Plinio Moreno, Jose Santos-Victor, Patricia Figueiredo, Athanasios Vourvopoulos

datasets.name: A steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI dataset in children and adolescents
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 47 neurotypical children and adolescents (5-18 years) who each completed a two-stage SSVEP-based brain-computer interface session. The session comprised a stimulus personalization pipeline followed by an online 4-target SSVEP game. Data were recorded with a 16-channel g.tec gel-based system at 256 Hz. The dataset was released by the BCI4Kids program to support signal-processing methods developed specifically for pediatric SSVEP-BCI data.
datasets.authors: Emily Schrag, Daniel Comaduran Marquez, Adam Kirton, Eli Kinney-Lang

datasets.name: Intracranial current source density (CSD) during epileptic seizures and interictal periods, one patient (Budapest)
datasets.description: Derivative dataset of intracranial current source density (CSD) traces from a single patient with drug-resistant epilepsy, implanted with subdural grid and strip electrodes at the National Institute for Clinical Neurosciences in Budapest. It contains 18 seizure segments and 16 interictal segments, each with 20480 samples at four sites (fronto-lateral Fl1 and Fl2, inferior-parietal iP, fronto-basal Fb). The data were used to infer causal relations between dynamical systems.
datasets.authors: Dániel Fabó, Loránd Erőss, Zsigmond Benkő

datasets.name: Medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex in approach-avoidance decisions (Starkweather et al., 2026): SEEG high-frequency activity, 6 patients (derivative)
datasets.description: This derivative dataset contains stereo-EEG high-frequency activity (HFA, 70-150 Hz) recorded from six patients with depth electrodes while they performed an approach-avoidance decision-making task. It supports analyses of the distinct contributions of medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex to decisions involving conflict. The data are the authors' processed HFA, repackaged in BIDS with trial-wise behavior, alignment-specific epochs and artifact-review labels, rather than raw iEEG.
datasets.authors: Clara Kwon Starkweather, Ethan H. Willbrand, Kristin K. Sellers, Patrick W. Hullett, Andrew D. Krystal, A. Moses Lee, Jon T. Willie, Peter Brunner, Ming Hsu, Edward F. Chang, Robert T. Knight

datasets.name: Electrophysiological signatures underlying variability in human memory consolidation: raw intracranial EEG (learning and sleep TMR)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from 11 patients with medically refractory temporal lobe epilepsy at Sanbo Brain Hospital, Beijing. Data were collected during learning of object-location associations and during targeted memory reactivation (TMR) with sounds in NREM sleep. The dataset supports investigation of electrophysiological signatures, such as hippocampal ripples and spindles, that underlie variability in human memory consolidation. It is a lossless BIDS re-packaging of the authors' raw Zenodo release.
datasets.authors: Wei Duan, Zhansheng Xu, Dong Chen, Jing Wang, Jiali Liu, Zheng Tan, Xue Xiao, Pengcheng Lv, Mengyang Wang, Ken A. Paller, Nikolai Axmacher, Liang Wang

datasets.name: Dataset of Speech Production in intracranial Electroencephalography (SingleWordProductionDutch-iBIDS)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings from 10 Dutch-speaking patients with pharmaco-resistant epilepsy who read aloud 100 Dutch words shown one at a time on a laptop screen. Intracranial EEG from 1103 contacts covering cortical and subcortical structures was recorded simultaneously with pitch-shifted speech audio. The dataset supports research on speech production, speech decoding and brain-computer interfaces, and includes electrode localisation and FreeSurfer derivatives.
datasets.authors: Maxime Verwoert, Maarten C. Ottenhoff, Sophocles Goulis, Albert J. Colon, Louis Wagner, Simon Tousseyn, Johannes P. van Dijk, Pieter L. Kubben, Christian Herff

datasets.name: Human intraoperative Neuropixels recordings, LF band (Paulk et al. 2022, DANDI 000397)
datasets.description: Local-field-potential (0.5-500 Hz, 2.5 kHz) band recordings from a single Neuropixels 1.0 thick-shank silicon probe (384 sites) inserted into human cortex during neurosurgery at Massachusetts General Hospital. The dataset comprises three task-free intraoperative recordings from the prefrontal cortex and anterior temporal lobe under general anesthesia or awake conditions. Data originate from Paulk et al. 2022 (DANDI 000397, Dryad) and are represented losslessly in iEEG-BIDS.
datasets.authors: Angelique C. Paulk, Yoav Kfir, Arjun R. Khanna, Martina L. Mustroph, Eric M. Trautmann, Dan J. Soper, Sergey D. Stavisky, Marleen Welkenhuysen, Barundeb Dutta, Krishna V. Shenoy, Leigh R. Hochberg, R. Mark Richardson, Ziv M. Williams, Sydney S. Cash

datasets.name: Sternberg working memory: human microwire LFP from medial temporal and medial frontal lobe (Daume et al. 2024, DANDI 000673)
datasets.description: Microwire local field potentials (LFP) recorded from Behnke-Fried hybrid depth electrodes in 35 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy during a picture-based Sternberg working-memory task (load 1 or 3). Recording sites include the hippocampus, amygdala, dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, pre-supplementary motor area and ventromedial prefrontal cortex. This iEEG-BIDS representation converts the DANDI 000673 NWB release (400 Hz LFP) without altering signal values, and includes trial, TTL marker and stimulus presentation events.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Daume, Jan Kaminski, Andrea G. P. Schjetnan, Yousef Salimpour, Umais Khan, Michael Kyzar, Chrystal M. Reed, William S. Anderson, Taufik A. Valiante, Adam N. Mamelak, Ueli Rutishauser

datasets.name: Cognitive boundaries and theta phase precession: human microwire LFP during movie-clip encoding, scene recognition and time discrimination (Zheng et al. 2024, DANDI 000940)
datasets.description: Microwire local field potentials recorded from Behnke-Fried hybrid depth electrodes in 16 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy during a cognitive-boundary memory paradigm. Participants encoded 90 silent movie clips containing no, soft, or hard event boundaries, then completed scene-recognition and time-discrimination tests. Recordings cover the amygdala, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus and several frontal sites, and were used to study hippocampal theta phase precession in memory formation and retrieval. This is an iEEG-BIDS representation of the authors' NWB release on DANDI (000940).
datasets.authors: Jie Zheng, Mar Yebra, Andrea G. P. Schjetnan, Kramay Patel, Chaim N. Katz, Michael Kyzar, Clayton P. Mosher, Suneil K. Kalia, Jeffrey M. Chung, Chrystal M. Reed, Taufik A. Valiante, Adam N. Mamelak, Gabriel Kreiman, Ueli Rutishauser

datasets.name: Intracranial recordings during Chinese word reading aloud in 12 patients with epilepsy: preprocessed task segments
datasets.description: Preprocessed stereo-EEG (sEEG) epochs from 12 patients with epilepsy reading 61 Chinese words aloud, packaged in BIDS from the Du-IN release. The data were band-pass filtered, resampled to 1000 Hz, bipolar re-referenced and segmented into 3-s word-labelled samples by the original authors. The dataset supports research on speech production and speech decoding from intracranial signals.
datasets.authors: Hui Zheng, Hai-Teng Wang, Wei-Bang Jiang, Zhong-Tao Chen, Li He, Pei-Yang Lin, Peng-Hu Wei, Guo-Guang Zhao, Yun-Zhe Liu

datasets.name: MNI Open iEEG Atlas: high-sampling-rate NREM sleep sEEG (normal high-frequency oscillations)
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG recordings of non-REM (N2/N3) sleep at original sampling rates (512, 1024 and 2000 Hz) from 71 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, released through the MNI Open iEEG Atlas. Only bipolar channels judged to show normal physiological activity in non-lesional grey matter are included (1152 channels), with Talairach coordinates and 17 brain-region labels. The data were used to derive normative values for ripples, fast ripples and high-frequency activity across brain regions.
datasets.authors: Birgit Frauscher, Nicolás von Ellenrieder, Rina Zelmann, Christine Rogers, Dang Khoa Nguyen, Philippe Kahane, François Dubeau, Jean Gotman

datasets.name: AJILE12: long-term naturalistic ECoG with wrist-movement events and behaviour labels (DANDI 000055)
datasets.description: AJILE12 comprises long-term naturalistic electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded opportunistically from 12 participants during clinical epilepsy monitoring at Harborview Medical Center, with simultaneous video. The dataset includes 55 day-long recordings with visually validated wrist-movement events and coarse behavioural state annotations, with no experimental task. This iEEG-BIDS representation was converted from the DANDI NWB release without altering signal values.
datasets.authors: Steven M. Peterson, Satpreet H. Singh, Benjamin Dichter, Michael Scheid, Rajesh P. N. Rao, Bingni W. Brunton

datasets.name: Movie watching and recognition memory: depth-electrode macro iEEG from Keles et al. 2024 (DANDI 000623)
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG recorded from clinical macroelectrode contacts of hybrid Behnke-Fried depth electrodes in 16 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing invasive monitoring. Participants passively watched an 8-minute edited excerpt of Hitchcock's "Bang! You're Dead" and then performed a new/old recognition memory test on 40 movie frames with confidence ratings. Electrodes targeted the amygdala, hippocampus and medial frontal cortex. This is an iEEG-BIDS conversion of the macroelectrode field potentials originally released in NWB format on DANDI (000623).
datasets.authors: Umit Keles, Julien Dubois, Kevin J. M. Le, J. Michael Tyszka, David A. Kahn, Chrystal M. Reed, Jeffrey M. Chung, Adam N. Mamelak, Ralph Adolphs, Ueli Rutishauser

datasets.name: Bellier et al. 2023 Pink Floyd music listening ECoG: authors' high-frequency activity (HFA, 70-150 Hz) for 29 patients
datasets.description: This dataset is a BIDS packaging of preprocessed electrocorticography (ECoG) high-frequency activity (HFA, 70-150 Hz) recorded from 29 patients with pharmacoresistant epilepsy while they passively listened to Pink Floyd's 'Another Brick in the Wall, Part 1'. It provides HFA envelopes at 100 Hz aligned to the 190.72 s song, together with MNI electrode coordinates and anatomical labels. The data derive from Bellier et al. (2023), who used them to reconstruct music from auditory cortex activity with nonlinear decoding models. Raw ECoG recordings and the stimulus audio are not included.
datasets.authors: Ludovic Bellier, Anaïs Llorens, Déborah Marciano, Aysegul Gunduz, Gerwin Schalk, Peter Brunner, Robert T. Knight

datasets.name: Schrag2026Pediatric: pediatric SSVEP-BCI dataset in children and adolescents
datasets.description: A pediatric steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface dataset recorded from 47 healthy children and adolescents aged 5-18 years. Each participant completed a stimulus personalization and comfort-rating procedure, then played an online four-target SSVEP-controlled game with both a personalized and a standard high-contrast stimulus. The 16-channel EEG recordings are provided in BIDS format with HED event annotations.
datasets.authors: Emily Schrag, Daniel Comaduran Marquez, Adam Kirton, Eli Kinney-Lang
